title: Prefinished vs Site-Finished Hardwood Floors: Cost, Look and Durability
meta: Prefinished hardwood installs at $3.25 per sq ft; site-finished runs $2.75 plus $3.99 to finish. Wills Flooring compares cost, look and durability in Edmonds.
keywords: prefinished vs site finished hardwood, prefinished vs unfinished hardwood flooring cost, site finished hardwood floors pros and cons, hardwood floor installation Edmonds WA, factory finished vs sanded in place
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Prefinished hardwood costs less in labor and is done in two days; site-finished costs more, takes a week, and gives you a seamless floor in any color that can be matched to what is already in the house.
blocks.detail: At Wills Flooring's published rates, prefinished installs at $3.25 per sq ft. Unfinished installs at $2.75 and then gets sanded and finished at $3.99 natural or $6.50 stained, so $6.74 to $9.25 per sq ft in labor and finish. Material is separate for both.

blocks.html: In Edmonds this decision usually comes with a second question attached: does it need to match the old floor? Half the homes we work in near the Bowl and in Seaview and Westgate have original 1950s to 70s oak somewhere, and the new floor is extending it into a kitchen or a former carpeted bedroom. That pushes the answer one way. A clean-slate remodel of a Perrinville rambler with no old wood to match pushes it the other. Here is how the two options compare on the three things people actually care about: money, look and how the floor holds up next to the Sound.

blocks.text: How the two floors look, up close and from the doorway

items.title: Micro-bevels and factory color
items.text: Each plank has a small beveled edge so slight height differences between boards do not show. From standing height it reads as fine lines across the floor. Colors are whatever the manufacturer offers this year, and the finish is identical from plank to plank.

items.title: One continuous surface
items.text: The floor is sanded flat as a single piece after installation, so there are no bevels and no lines. Finish flows across every seam and seals them. This is the look of an original Edmonds Bowl floor, and the only way to make a new room match one.

items.title: Color control
items.text: Site-finished means any stain, any sheen, tested on your own boards under your own light. Waterfront rooms in Edmonds get strong low afternoon light off the water, and the ability to sample three tones in place before committing is worth a lot.

items.title: Matching existing wood
items.text: If you are adding new oak next to 60-year-old oak, prefinished will never match: the bevels, the color and the sheen all differ. Unfinished boards woven in and sanded with the old floor become one floor. See our post on matching new hardwood to old for how we do it.

blocks.text: Durability: factory finish vs finish applied in your house

a.title: Strengths and weaknesses
items: Aluminum-oxide factory finish is harder than anything applied on site and resists scratches longer
Cured under UV lamps, so it is at full hardness on day one
Seams are unsealed, so a spill can wick between boards and under the finish
Recoating later is harder because the bevels trap old finish and dirt
Board-by-board replacement is easy if you keep a spare carton

b.title: Strengths and weaknesses
items: Three coats of Bona water-based finish seal the seams, which matters in a wet Edmonds kitchen
Can be screened and recoated at $1.99 per sq ft every 7 to 10 years to stay new
Softer than aluminum oxide in the first month while it cures fully
Quality depends entirely on the crew; Wills are Bona Certified Craftsmen
Any future repair is sanded and blended, not swapped

blocks.title: The Edmonds humidity angle:
blocks.text: Homes in the Bowl and along the bluff sit in marine air most of the year. Unsealed seams on a prefinished floor let that moisture cycle in and out of the board edges, which is where cupping starts. A site-finished floor's sealed seams slow that down. It is not a reason to avoid prefinished, but it is a reason to pick a prefinished floor with a good factory-sealed edge and to keep the house between 35 and 50 percent humidity.

items.text: Acclimate 48 to 72 hours, install, done. Walk on it the same evening. Furniture back the next day. Ideal for a Seaview family that cannot be out of the kitchen for a week.
items.note: 800 sq ft: about two days on site

items.text: Acclimate three to seven days, then install the raw boards over two days. The floor is walkable but bare.
Sand flat, fill, stain if chosen, then three coats of finish. Rooms are closed. Socks after 24 hours from the last coat, furniture after 72, rugs after two weeks.
items.note: 800 sq ft: about six to seven working days plus acclimation

blocks.text: Which one is wrong for your house

items.html: Prefinished is the wrong call when you are extending or repairing an existing hardwood floor, when you want a custom color or sheen, or when the room is a kitchen with a dishwasher and a history of small leaks.

Site-finished is the wrong call when you need to be back in the room in two days, when the budget is tight and the floor is standalone, or when the house cannot handle a week of dust and closed rooms. Many Edmonds retirees downsizing into a Westgate rambler pick prefinished for exactly this reason.
Engineered prefinished is the right call over a slab or in a condo where nail-down is impossible. Site-finished engineered exists but is rare.
A hybrid works too. Prefinished in bedrooms, site-finished in the main living area where it meets the original floor. We do this often in older Edmonds homes.

blocks.text: What to ask before you sign either quote

items.html: Is the finish line separate? A site-finished quote should show installation and refinishing as two rates, the way our hardwood installation page does, so you can compare apples to apples.
Can I see stain samples on my boards? For site-finished, yes, always, on a spare board in your light. For prefinished, ask for a full plank, not a chip.
Who is doing the finish? Ask for the certification. Wills Flooring are Bona Certified Craftsmen and every install and finish carries a 1-year workmanship warranty.
What edge does the prefinished plank have? Micro-bevel, eased or square. Square-edge prefinished is closest to a site-finished look but shows height differences more.

faq.q: Is prefinished or site-finished hardwood cheaper?
faq.a: Prefinished is cheaper in labor. Wills Flooring installs it at $3.25 per sq ft. Site-finished is $2.75 to install plus $3.99 to sand and finish natural, or $6.50 with stain, so $6.74 to $9.25 per sq ft. Unfinished planks cost less than prefinished, which closes part of that gap.

faq.q: Which lasts longer, prefinished or site-finished hardwood?
faq.a: The aluminum-oxide factory finish on prefinished floors is harder and resists scratches longer at first. Site-finished floors have sealed seams and can be recoated at $1.99 per sq ft every several years, so they can be kept looking new almost indefinitely. Both are solid wood that lasts decades.

faq.q: Can you refinish prefinished hardwood floors?
faq.a: Yes. Solid prefinished floors and engineered floors with a thick enough wear layer can be fully sanded and refinished later, which removes the bevels and turns them into a site-finished floor. A simple recoat is harder on prefinished because dirt and old finish sit in the bevel lines.

It looks more seamless. There are no bevel lines, the finish covers every seam, and the color is custom. Whether that is better depends on taste; many buyers like the crisp plank definition of a prefinished floor. In older Edmonds homes with original oak, site-finished is the only way to match.

faq.q: How long does site-finished hardwood take compared to prefinished?
faq.a: Prefinished is walkable the day it goes in, about two days for a main floor after a short acclimation. Site-finished takes six to seven working days for the same area: two to install, one to sand, and three for stain and finish coats, plus longer acclimation for the raw boards.

faq.q: Is prefinished hardwood okay in a kitchen?
faq.a: Yes, with care. The unsealed seams between prefinished planks can let a spill or dishwasher leak wick between boards. Wipe spills quickly and choose a plank with a factory-sealed edge. For a kitchen that has already had a leak, site-finished with sealed seams is the safer choice.
